title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Ten named destinations along streets just beyond Illinois Tech, each offering one specific reason to explore Bronzeville, Armour Square, or Bridgeport.

cards.title: Read Poetry Cast in Bronze
cards.subtitle: East 31st Street at Dunbar Park
cards.notes: Walk east on 31st Street and inspect Debra Hand’s bronze portrait; Dunbar’s poem “Dreams” is incorporated into the seating wall.
cards.short_summary: A literary monument turns a park stop into a close-reading exercise.
cards.evidence_claim: The Park District identifies this as Debra Hand’s 2014 bronze monument and says text from Dunbar’s poem “Dreams” appears in an adjacent seating wall.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor monument at 300 E. 31st Street within Dunbar Park; park hours are 6:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m. daily.

cards.title: Take 31st Street to the Lake
cards.subtitle: East 31st Street lakefront corridor
cards.notes: Follow 31st Street toward the lake for the skyline view, then use the beach house restrooms or the adjacent accessible playground.
cards.short_summary: The campus-side east-west street ends at a named beach and broad skyline view.
cards.evidence_claim: The Park District says Margaret T. Burroughs Beach, often called 31st Street Beach, provides skyline views, restrooms, an ADA-accessible playground, and a public fishing dock.
cards.access_notes: Check posted swimming status and seasonal lifeguard information before entering the water; other lakefront features have separate access conditions.

cards.title: Frame the Ballpark from the Courts
cards.subtitle: South Shields Avenue near 33rd Street
cards.notes: Head to Shields Avenue for an outdoor pause among the tennis courts, playground, and picnic areas, with the neighboring stadium in view.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood recreation complex supplies an active counterpoint to the nearby stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: The Park District lists Armour Square Park at 3309 South Shields Avenue and documents tennis courts, a playground, picnic space, and other recreation facilities.
cards.access_notes: Park hours are 6:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. daily; individual indoor facilities and programs may follow different schedules.

cards.title: Find the Defender’s Former Home
cards.subtitle: South Indiana Avenue near 35th Street
cards.notes: Pause at 3435 South Indiana Avenue to study the landmark exterior that housed the Chicago Defender during four pivotal decades.
cards.short_summary: A former synagogue marks the newspaper address tied to the Great Migration.
cards.evidence_claim: Chicago’s landmarks database says the building at 3435 South Indiana Avenue housed the Chicago Defender from 1920 to 1960 and is part of the Black Metropolis-Bronzeville Historic District.
cards.access_notes: Treat this as an exterior architecture stop; the landmark listing does not establish public interior access.

cards.title: Meet the Eighth Regiment Memorial
cards.subtitle: East 35th Street at Martin Luther King Drive
cards.notes: Stop at the 35th Street median and examine the bronze panels and soldier created to honor the Eighth Regiment’s First World War service.
cards.short_summary: A prominent median monument records Black military history in Bronzeville.
cards.evidence_claim: Chicago’s landmarks database places the Victory Monument at 35th Street and King Drive and says it honors the African American Eighth Regiment of the Illinois National Guard.
cards.access_notes: View from legal pedestrian areas and use marked crossings; the monument occupies the King Drive median.

cards.title: See the South Side Ballpark
cards.subtitle: West 35th Street at South Shields Avenue
cards.notes: Walk west along 35th Street to photograph the ballpark exterior and compare its large-scale structure with Illinois Tech’s campus architecture.
cards.short_summary: The 35th Street stadium creates a sharp change in scale just west of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Illinois Sports Facilities Authority identifies Rate Field at 333 West 35th Street and describes it as an event and production venue.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is the default; games, tours, and special events may require tickets and operate on event-specific schedules.

cards.title: Enter a Former Warehouse Arts Hub
cards.subtitle: West 35th Street at South Racine Avenue
cards.notes: Continue west on 35th Street and check the center’s current calendar before visiting its galleries, studios, or sculpture-garden spaces.
cards.short_summary: An industrial building extends the 35th Street trip into working art spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Bridgeport Art Center’s official materials locate it at 1200 West 35th Street and describe galleries, artist studios, and a sculpture-garden event space.
cards.access_notes: Public access varies by gallery exhibition, open-studio event, and private booking; confirm the current calendar before departure.

cards.title: Step Inside a Newspaper Landmark
cards.subtitle: South State Street at 36th Place
cards.notes: Walk south on State Street to examine the Art Deco exterior, then enter during branch hours to see its public-art collection.
cards.short_summary: A historic publishing building now serves Bronzeville as a public library.
cards.evidence_claim: Chicago Public Library says the Chicago Bee Branch occupies the Art Deco Chicago Bee building and features works by Gregg Spears, Derek Webster, and Carrie Mae Weems.
cards.access_notes: Library services and interior access follow current branch hours; consult the linked branch page before visiting.

cards.entity_name: The Light of Truth: Ida B. Wells National Monument
cards.title: Circle Richard Hunt’s Wells Monument
cards.subtitle: South Langley Avenue near 37th Street
cards.notes: Turn onto Langley Avenue and walk around Richard Hunt’s sculptural installation to view its granite, bronze, and inscribed elements.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated plaza commemorates Ida B. Wells through monumental public art.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chicago Literary Hall of Fame identifies the monument at 3739 South Langley Avenue as a Richard Hunt work on the former Ida B. Wells Homes site and part of Chicago’s public-art collection.
cards.source_title: Ida B. Wells Monument: Light of Truth
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor plaza stop; use public sidewalks and observe any posted site conditions.

cards.title: Choose a One-Acre Activity Break
cards.subtitle: South Prairie Avenue near 38th Street
cards.notes: Use Prairie Avenue for a compact recreation stop with outdoor basketball, tennis, a playground, garden, and public artwork in one block.
cards.short_summary: A small park concentrates several active and visual options east of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Park District places Anderson Park at 3748 South Prairie Avenue and lists basketball courts, tennis courts, a playground, harvest garden, and mosaic among its facilities.
cards.access_notes: Park hours are 6:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m. daily; the fieldhouse and organized programs maintain separate schedules.
